title: POC Weekly Sync: Rollout & Go-live Planning
summary: Weekly POC sync to review pilot results, finalize canary and A/B rollouts, agree cutover MOP, monitoring/alerting, and outstanding security items. Benchmarks looked good for 90% of workloads; edge cases around long invoice threads causing KV cache growth. Agreed near-term plan: 2-week canary with 10% traffic, runbook + rollback steps, final SLA targets, Redwood to send runbook template, security docs, and updated pricing for Dedicated burst option.
topics: Canary deployment strategy and percentage ramps
Cutover checklist and MOP (method of procedure)
Security/compliance items: KMS, audit logs, SSO
Benchmark findings: latency percentiles and cost tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-14 10:00 PT — Duration 45m. Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonas (Redwood SE), Priya (AtlasPayments Head of Platform), Evan (Eng Manager), Liam (SRE), Sara (Security).

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining tight agenda today is roll out planning, canary, cutover, monitoring, runbooks, also security signoffs. i know you had some bench results earlier this week - priya want to kick us off?

[00:18] Priya (AtlasPayments): yeah thanks maya. overall the pilot looks good, we saw p50 around 80ms and p95 around 220ms on the typical payment flow which matches what you shared in the benchmark. there are some outliers for long invoice history threads, latency spikes up to 850ms.

[00:36] Jonas (Redwood SE): right, that's the KV cache / prefix growth case we flagged — when users request long conversational context the kv cache warms and memory pressure can cause slight eviction thrash. we have two quick mitigations: quantization-friendly model variant and aggressive prefix truncation for that route.

[00:55] Evan (AtlasPayments): aggressive prefix truncation worries product — we don't want to drop necessary context for dispute flows. can we do route-level overrides?

[01:10] Jonas: yes per-route config is supported — you can keep the dispute route at full context and apply truncation elsewhere; also suggestion to use dynamic caching TTLs.

[01:26] Liam (SRE): for the canary we want clear rollback triggers — CPU/GPU oversubscription, error rate > 1.5% sustained for 5m, or p95 latency > 500ms for two consecutive 5m windows. are those acceptable?

[01:42] Maya: seems reasonable, we recommend starting with conservative thresholds and relax after 48h of stable metrics. for canary percent, propose 10% for 48h, then 25% for 24h, then 50% if stable, final cutover at 7 days.

[01:58] Priya: 10% for 48h is fine. question about traffic split — we want sticky routing so a user in canary stays in canary to avoid inconsistent experiences.

[02:12] Jonas: we support sticky session routing based on cookie or header; we'll share config examples. note: sticky routing increases cache variance but is typically fine.

[02:30] Sara (Security): from security side, remaining items: KMS integration verification, audit log retention policy, and SSO/SAML test with Okta. we have SOC 2 requirements and need proof of logging for tokens and model versioning.

[02:45] Maya: we will send the security pack — KMS integration guide, sample audit logs, and SSO steps. Jonas will follow up on model version metadata included in logs.

[03:00] Evan: what about Dedicated vs Hosted for go-live? cost / latency tradeoffs again.

[03:08] Maya: two options: stay Hosted on Redwood API with reserved Dedicated burst for peak nights (we gave a pricing delta) or migrate to Redwood Dedicated for steady throughput. For go-live (first 3 months) many customers run Hosted + burst to avoid heavy ops, then decide. we'll re-send the pricing with burst numbers included.

[03:30] Priya: timeline: finance needs a 30-day window to sign up dedicated capacity if we choose that. so we should plan for hosted canary first.

[03:40] Liam: monitoring — what dashboards and alerts should we put in place for canary?

[03:46] Jonas: recommended dashboards: per-route QPS, p50/p95/p99 latencies, error rates, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, and model token counts (cost signal). alerts: error-rate, p95 spike, and token-per-request anomaly. we'll send canned Grafana dashboards and alert templates.

[04:10] Maya: also add healthcheck endpoints and a synthetic job we can run every minute to detect regressions. add canary-specific logs to a separate index for easier pivoting.

[04:24] Priya: runbook — need a step-by-step MOP for cutover and rollback. what granularity do you provide?

[04:31] Jonas: we have a runbook template with step 0 validations, pre-cutover checks (capacity, keys, routes), canary ramp plan, rollback commands, and post-cutover validation scripts. we'll share the template and can fill in Atlas-specific commands.

[04:50] Evan: also want automated fallback: if canary fails, direct traffic back to previous model and send incident to slack channel. is that supported?

[04:58] Maya: yes automatic fallback policies exist — you can set thresholds to trigger fallback to a compatible variant or to a hosted lower-cost model. fallback is tracked in audit logs.

[05:12] Sara: a note on compliance: we need data residency and logs retention settings documented — even if hosted, logs must be retained for 1 year for this business unit.

[05:22] Maya: noted, we'll include retention settings in the security pack.

[05:30] Priya: ok items for next two weeks? canary start ideally Monday next week if we get runbook and security signoff by Friday.

[05:40] Jonas: we'll prepare a 2-week canary MOP: day-by-day ramp, synthetic tests, acceptance criteria. also will run a 24h stress test on your staging traffic to validate p95 under load.

[05:55] Liam: schedule the synthetic tests to run in our staging with a shadow traffic option — avoid hitting billing.

[06:04] Maya: agreed shadow mode for staging. we'll also provide a test payload set.

[06:12] Priya: any outstanding technical risks?

[06:16] Jonas: main ones: long-context KV growth (mitigations noted), and token cost on chatty workflows. we recommend a cache TTL and fine-grained per-route cost alert.

[06:30] Evan: for cost, can we set per-route quotas or throttles?

[06:34] Maya: yes we support per-route quotas and rate limits, plus token budgets for keys. we'll send config examples.

[06:45] Priya: thanks. let's recap next steps.

[06:50] Maya: recap: Redwood to send runbook template, security pack (KMS, logs, SSO), canned dashboards + alert rules, updated pricing with Dedicated burst numbers, and a staging test payload. Atlas to review and sign security items by Friday; aim to start 10% canary Monday.

[07:12] Evan: i'll own the signoff and coordinate with finance for dedicated decision timeline.

[07:20] Liam: i'll run the staging shadow test with your payload once delivered.

[07:26] Sara: i'll validate KMS and retention requirements once we get the docs.

[07:32] Maya: perfect. we'll follow-up with calendar invites for the cutover window and send the artifact links.

[07:40] Meeting ends
